_note: Frozen content for design review. Comparison family — every page sets the common approach against the one that holds up, both sides carrying identical structure so the split fills symmetrically.
brief: Six habits that look professional and quietly cost you the job

slots.titleLine1: Everything you were taught to do
slots.body: Not because it is wrong, but because it was taught by people who were competing against a different room.
slots.badClaim: Look prepared, look senior, look certain.
slots.goodClaim: Be the only person who names the real problem.
slots.bad1: Rewards the person who sounds most certain.
slots.good1: Rewards the person who is most useful to think with.
slots.bad2: Taught in rooms where everyone had the same training.
slots.good2: Works in rooms where nobody has read the same book.

slots.titleLine1: Presenting three options is not generosity
slots.badClaim: Show three directions and let the client choose.
slots.bad1: Reads as an unwillingness to commit to a view.
slots.bad2: Splits the room, because everyone picks a different one.
slots.bad3: Triples the work and gets paid for one of them.
slots.goodClaim: Show one, and show what you rejected.
slots.good1: A recommendation is what they are paying you for.
slots.good2: The rejected work proves the choice was considered.
slots.good3: The conversation becomes why, not which.
slots.body: Three options moves the decision to the person with the least context. That is not service, it is abdication.

slots.titleLine1: Nobody has ever been reassured by a status report
slots.badClaim: Send a summary of everything that happened.
slots.bad1: Volume reads as effort, not as progress.
slots.bad2: Buries the one thing they needed to know.
slots.bad3: Takes an afternoon and gets skimmed in nine seconds.
slots.goodClaim: Send what changed and what you need.
slots.good1: Three lines, sent on the day it happened.
slots.good2: Bad news first, while it is still cheap.
slots.good3: Ends with a question or it ends with nothing.
slots.body: The update exists to prevent surprises, not to prove work happened. Anything longer is proving.

slots.titleLine1: Being right in the room is worth almost nothing
slots.badClaim: Win the argument with the better case.
slots.bad1: Nobody changes position in front of an audience.
slots.bad2: The loser now has a reason to be right later.
slots.bad3: The decision reverses quietly the following week.
slots.goodClaim: Make the case before the room exists.
slots.good1: One conversation each, ahead of the meeting.
slots.good2: People defend positions they helped shape.
slots.good3: The meeting becomes a confirmation, not a fight.
slots.body: Meetings do not decide, they ratify. The decision was made in the conversations before it.

slots.titleLine1: A confident number is not a useful one
slots.badClaim: Give a single date and defend it.
slots.bad1: Sounds decisive and is wrong about half the time.
slots.bad2: Every slip becomes a broken promise.
slots.bad3: Encourages padding, which nobody believes anyway.
slots.goodClaim: Give a range and what would narrow it.
slots.good1: Names the unknown instead of pricing it invisibly.
slots.good2: Turns a deadline into a shared problem.
slots.good3: Updating a range is normal; moving a date is a failure.
slots.body: The date was never the deliverable. Knowing when it will be knowable is.

slots.titleLine1: Work only you can run is not an achievement
slots.badClaim: Stay the person who knows how it works.
slots.bad1: Feels like security and functions like a ceiling.
slots.bad3: You get kept in the role you are best at escaping.
slots.good1: Write it down for a competent stranger in a hurry.
slots.good2: Watch someone else run it once, saying nothing.
slots.good3: Being replaceable is what makes you promotable.
slots.body: Indispensable is a compliment people pay you right before they stop considering you for anything else.

slots.titleLine1: None of this works if the work is not good
slots.badClaim: Communicate well enough and the work is forgiven.
slots.bad2: Referrals stop before anyone tells you why.
slots.bad3: The reputation arrives before you do, either way.
slots.goodClaim: These make good work land. Nothing more.
slots.good1: They remove the reasons good work gets rejected.
slots.good2: They cannot manufacture a reason to be chosen.
slots.good3: The craft is still the only durable part.
slots.body: Every habit here raises the ceiling on work that is already good. None of them raises the floor.

slots.eyebrow: Try one on the next thing you send
slots.body: The habit you would defend hardest is usually the one doing the most damage, because defending it is how it survived this long.
slots.badClaim: Change the update. Nobody will object.
slots.goodClaim: Show one direction and stand behind it.
slots.signoff: The nervous one is the one that changes something
slots.bad1: Low risk, and nobody will thank you for it.
slots.good1: Feels exposed, and it is the one that gets remembered.
slots.bad2: You can do it this afternoon.
slots.good2: You will put it off until something forces it.
